- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-95+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to correct downward.
- Shows persistent lag in responding to recent price declines — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate gradual pullback after peaks.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to adjust for volatility clustering or policy-induced shocks.
- Tends to overfit recent high volatility periods, leading to erratic forecasts when market stabilizes.
- Underestimates downward pressure in low-price regimes (e.g., <85), often missing the “floor” effect.
- Sensitive to initial conditions — forecasts drift downward if history contains a prolonged downtrend.
